commitments.text:
Based on the March 17-20, 2004 yield test on PW#5 Kala provides the following conclusions:
a) Based on a review of all identified domestic water wells within the cone of depression of PW#5 during half day pumping cycles there are three existing local water wells which may experience problems due to pumping interference: Mills (#42), Bains (#24) and Krane Logging (#32) as shown in Figure 6. Each of the wells are constructed with well depths close to the static water levels which minimizes total available drawdown (TAD) and the wells are typically less than 38 m deep. These wells are older (>20 years each). Drawdown interference from PW#5 may serve to exacerbate the limited TAD problems. All other wells currently constructed within the 0.0 drawdown contour will not be impacted by drawdown interference based on the Kala review chiefly due to their deeper completion depths. As PW#4 will not and can not be operated at the same time as PW#5 collective drawdown interference will not be a concern.

3) Gather data to confirm the accuracy of the current model and to provide calibration data for further refinement of the model.
Combining the data collected by the city with information from other monitoring programs will allow the City, the Regional District, and the Province to better understand and predict the performance of the aquifers in question under stressed (i.e. drought) conditions. The City of Cranbrook’s well monitoring program will be maintained by the Engineering and Works Departments.
The monitoring program consists of regular monitoring of the municipal production wells, the observation wells sited 6 meters from the production wells, and eight private wells in the area near the Cobham well. The private wells were selected by Kala Groundwater based on:
• Ease of access
• Age/condition of the well
• Depth of the well
• Distance from the Cobham well
• Representative nature of the well
• Permission of the owner to enter the property
The monitoring program began prior to commissioning of the wells and has continued on a weekly basis. Information collected at the private wells is as follows:
• Cobham Flowrate
• Cobham Pump on/off
• Water level from surface
• Time of day
• Date
Based on the observations obtained during the long term monitoring, the program will be refined or expanded by the City as deemed necessary.
In addition to the level monitoring program, water quality is sampled and analyzed weekly when the pumps are in operation. The water quality data will not only meet health requirements but will provide an indication if there is any change in groundwater chemistry.
The proposed pump stations are provided with monitoring equipment which will record the following parameters on a 24 hr basis:
- water level in the wells
- flows
- main pressures
- chlorine demand
- intruder alarm
- interior temperature alarm
- low water level alarm
The City will work co-operatively with local staff of the Ministries of Water, Land and Air Protection and of Sustainable Resources Management to share groundwater data and other resources where practical.
